# 油價反彈逆轉美債漲勢，信用買家抗拒利差過度收窄

## 消費轉弱，仍未能壓住收盤殖利率

零售銷售與消費信心疲弱，一度帶動美債上漲；美國再對伊朗發出威脅、油價走高後，行情卻反轉。2年期殖利率盤中短暫跌破4.10%，創6月30日以來最低，最後反而上升2個基點至4.17%。5年、10年及30年期分別上升4、5及4個基點，收在4.36%、4.68%及5.25%。曲線轉陡，2年與10年期利差擴大3個基點至51個基點，2年與30年期擴大2個基點至108個基點。

7月零售銷售下降0.6%，為2025年5月以來最大跌幅；8月密西根大學消費信心初值僅51，低於預期。Goolsbee也因通膨改善而支持耐心觀察。這些消息減輕近期升息的理由，但財長貝森特承諾對伊朗施加前所未有的經濟壓力，讓焦點回到能源。WTI上漲1.42%至$82.40，布蘭特上漲1.67%至$88.52；10年期損益兩平通膨率上升3個基點至2.27%，實質殖利率升2個基點至2.41%。

密集發債後，信用投資人也開始抗拒讓利縮水。投資級借款人兩週內已籌得$1,360億，承銷團收窄最終定價時，訂單平均較初始簿冊減少36%，是前一週的兩倍，也高於全年平均22%。基金仍吸金近$30億，利差維持約78個基點；市場不缺現金，爭點在買方願意放棄多少新券溢價。

這場議價不只發生在一般公司債。AI融資日益仰賴保證，景氣反轉時可能把損失帶回晶片商；Zenith Arc雖有Jane Street長租約，資料中心債仍在預期區間較高殖利率端定價。其他借款人則以股本籌資，或因擔保品移轉遭債權人挑戰。市場持續提供融資，條件卻愈來愈取決於損失最終由哪張資產負債表承擔。

## 消費降溫，油價與長期借款成本卻形成反向壓力

7月零售13類中有五類下降。包括網購在內的非店面銷售減少2.2%，汽車及零件銷售減少1.8%；報告中唯一的服務類別、餐廳與酒吧則增加0.5%。數據未經通膨調整，Amazon將Prime Day由去年7月提前至今年6月，也可能讓部分網購提早發生。即使考量這項時點因素，消費在較強的上半年後仍顯得較無韌性。

密西根大學消費信心初值51，相較市場共識55。搭配招聘轉弱與本週通膨數據，政策定價延續8月7日以來的調整。短率合約對9月緊縮僅反映約8個基點，低於7月31日的近19個基點；市場也逐漸放棄2027年中前升息超過一次的預期。早盤2年期上漲確實反映政策路徑改變，只是未能維持至收盤。

Goolsbee形容經濟與勞動市場基本穩定，但若零售銷售連續數月下滑，會讓他擔心。通膨仍是首要問題。他歡迎先前五、六個月不利走勢後，最近三個月出現改善，並表示若再有三、四次像6月的讀數，對通膨回到2%會更有信心。7月已連續第五次維持利率，仍有三位官員主張升息25個基點；一次弱消費數據尚未化解分歧。

他也質疑，生產力在去年強勁表現後減速，究竟是否暫時現象。AI可能提高供給能力、降低單位成本，投資熱潮卻也可能使需求過熱。Fed因此須同時評估未來效率提升，以及當前設備、電力與建設支出，不能把科技一概視為壓低通膨的力量。

貝森特表示，美國下週將宣布經濟孤立史上前所未有的措施，並持續海軍封鎖伊朗港口。消息在收盤前傳出，逆轉了消費轉弱帶來的利多。布蘭特近一週上漲5.95%，WTI上漲5.40%。10年期通膨補償當日增加3個基點，不僅收復週四跌幅，更回到8月11日水準；實質殖利率上升則增加另一層壓力。

本週標售後，長期融資成本仍居高不下。30年期收盤殖利率已高於5.216%的得標利率，10年期也幾乎回到自身標售定價。近一個月10年及30年期名目殖利率分別上升10與17個基點，2年期則下降1個基點，2年與30年期曲線轉陡18個基點。10年期實質殖利率為2.41%、月升8個基點，30年期為3.00%、月升13個基點。

標售證明高利率下仍有需求，並未解決赤字或增加中的民間投資需求。財政部討論過調整發行，尚未縮減長債供給；將更多債務移至2年至7年期，可改變存續期間及再融資曝險，卻不會減少總借款需求。

美債按原始面額計算的總成交額為$9,745億，較週四減少19.0%，其中名目附息債為$8,244億。20年以上成交仍增加3.3%至$1,168億，交易商對客戶占該區間50.7%。長端殖利率上升時，市場仍有相當參與度，並非單純缺乏交易。

能源反轉對股市影響較小。S&P 500下跌0.17%，Nasdaq 100跌0.13%，VIX卻下降2.60%至14.25。黃金上漲0.39%至$4,380.40，美元指數下跌0.29%至99.67。債市承受較多通膨疑慮，但未伴隨全面美元緊縮或股市撤退。

## 信用買家手上有錢，但要求保留新券溢價

訂單流失讓初級市場的轉變具體可見。本週平均36%，比2026年常態高14個百分點，週四45%更創今年最高。AMD在$47.5億發行中收窄定價後，最長年期訂單減少逾半。交易仍順利完成，但初始訂單簿不代表投資人願意接受任何利差。

兩週$1,360億供給讓8月有望創歷來同期紀錄，下週預計才會降至約$200億。併購融資、AI基礎設施與一般再融資同時進場，美債又提供高實質殖利率。替代選擇增加，買方接受極小新券溢價的機會成本也跟著提高。

截至週三的一週，投資級基金流入近$30億，平均利差約78個基點。HYG與JNK週五僅跌0.10%及0.07%，近一週仍略為正報酬；LQD則隨基準殖利率上升而跌0.40%。這與全面出清相去甚遠，更值得觀察的是發行人壓低初始利差後，還有多少訂單留下。

Zenith Arc提供了專案融資的例子。$22.5億5年期Ba2綠色債券以99.5定價，殖利率近9%，落在早先討論區間較高的一端。Jane Street子公司的15年三重淨租約及慣常集團保證，將營運費、稅金、水電、保險及電力成本交由租戶負擔。即使有這些支持，投資人對施工、技術及集中曝險仍要求區間較高的報酬。

## AI保證可能將損失帶回供應商

Nvidia擬與高盛、黑石及Apollo合作，促成最高$5,000億運算投資。黃仁勳已說明，可逐案提供最高為投資機會25%的殘值支持。這個上限限制單一專案承諾，但客戶無力付款與設備跌價若同時發生，風險仍會彼此牽動。

有殘值保證後，SPV可以設備與合約支持，以較低成本借款。客戶若停付，硬體可重新出租或出售，剩餘缺口由保證人負擔。債務隨晶片折舊攤還，通常約五年，保證規模因而下降；但客戶違約與二手設備價格下跌同時出現時，保障才最重要，而同一波景氣下行也可能削弱晶片商本身獲利。

Meta在路易斯安那州Hyperion約$270億融資，以及德州Sopaipilla約$130億方案中使用殘值支持，責任與其選擇提早退出長租約相關。Broadcom則為Anthropic的$350億Big Sky晶片融資提供大部分保障。美銀策略師估計，較廣泛的AI XPV平台至2029年中可能累積$3,700億優先債務。各架構條件不同，不能全部視為同一種公司負債。

標普在調整後槓桿中，將Broadcom支持視為類似債務的或有義務；穆迪也警告，即使帳面負債不高，短期內多筆交易仍可能降低財務彈性。目前已有約$700億此類或有支持未列入大型公司的帳面債務。擴張期，它以供應商很少的即時現金支出，降低客戶採購成本；下行期，卻可能在獲利與設備價值同步惡化時把損失帶回。評估信用因此不能只看已發行債券，還須考量客戶、擔保品與保證人之間的相關性。

## 擔保品爭議與股本交易，改變債權人承擔的風險

Arini與GoldenTree擴大對Liberty Puerto Rico的訴訟，挑戰5月議定的$1.4億循環信貸及$2億定期貸款。債權人指控，這些融資以9月負債管理交易中移至非受限子公司的資產作擔保；早先交易已把公司多數資產移出既有貸款人可追索範圍，用以支持Diameter Capital Partners的$2.5億新債。AllianceBernstein關係企業、Octagon Credit Investors及MacKay Shields也加入紐約州最高法院案件。

修正後訴狀另提及，未取得對價便取消的公司間貸款，以及5月發行的$5億特別股，後者可能每年支付Liberty Latin America股東$4,500萬股息。這些是有爭議的指控，而非法院判決，涉及擔保品移轉、支付順位與股東分配。案件將檢驗非受限子公司條款及新融資，能在多大程度上改變舊貸款人的回收。

Dangote Sugar則以股本修復資產負債表。公司在超額認購的現金增資中，以每股NGN60發行81億股，籌得NGN4,860億、約$3.56億。資金將減債、補回三年虧損侵蝕的資本，並支持營運與向上游整合。奈及利亞2023年貨幣貶值推高融資及投入成本，公司曾陷入淨值為負，之後才恢復。既有股東接受稀釋，換取企業及債權人可運用資源增加。

Kedrion Biopharma考慮的是另一種資金用途：約€20億私人債務，部分用來支付Permira及阿布達比投資局等所有人股利。這家血漿治療公司營收逾€15億，但條件與最終決定仍在討論。長期併購低迷後，私人貸款人資金充裕，可能支持交易；不過，相同金額若用於分配股東而非生產性擴張，留給債權人的緩衝不同，最終槓桿與文件條款仍重要。

## 印尼承諾縮減赤字，中國融資更仰賴公部門

印尼總統Prabowo Subianto將2027年赤字目標設為GDP的2.4%，低於2026年預估2.85%。支出將增加4%至IDR4,097兆，收入成長7%，假設匯率每美元IDR17,500、原油$75。週五印尼盾與股市上漲，債券殖利率下降。

較低赤字仍須靠執行。上半年政府支出增加近30%，協助經濟成長5.45%，為13年來最強上半年表現；前一年的赤字目標卻已修正至接近3%法定上限。採購節省、國營企業股利與收入成長，現在必須支應食品、能源、教育及鄉村方案，避免再次上修。公布目標有利市場，但不代表節省已經實現。

肯亞計畫年底12月前發行$8.15億歐洲債券，納入截至2027年6月的$54億外部融資方案。其他項目包括$3億熊貓債、$5億伊斯蘭債券，以及與世界糧食計畫署合作、由美國國際開發金融公司支持的$10億債務換糧食方案。財長John Mbadi另打算償還至少$5億昂貴外債。IMF將肯亞列為高度債務困境風險國家，因此替換高成本負債，與取得新資金同樣重要。

中國融資數據顯示，公部門借款正在替代疲弱的民間需求。7月實體經濟人民幣貸款淨償還CNY5,900億，為2002年有資料以來最大收縮；包括金融機構間信用的整體貸款減少CNY3,400億，逾預期降幅三倍。社會融資仍增加CNY1.4兆，但政府債券占CNY1.3兆。家庭與企業中長期貸款都收縮，房市需求弱、薪資停滯與預期報酬低，促使借款人減債。

人民銀行進行CNY3,490億隔夜逆回購，淨投放CNY3,480億，首次在月中使用這個年期。這是先前未進行其他公開市場投放後，回應繳稅資金需求，並非宣布全面寬鬆。另一筆CNY1兆6個月買斷式逆回購，只替換等額到期。中國10年期公債殖利率下跌1個基點至1.68%，創2025年7月以來最低，10年期標售利率也為一年多來最低。精準資金支持可穩定貨幣市場，卻未必能逆轉民間借款的紀錄性疲弱。

## 行情反轉後，接著看制裁細節與20年期標售

8月26日核心PCE、其間的就業數據及Warsh傑克森洞發言，將顯示有利通膨讀數累積是否已足夠長，能滿足Goolsbee的要求。需求持續偏弱、服務物價溫和與招聘降溫，有助政策敏感年期，即使長期資金仍昂貴；消費反彈或通膨擴散，則會讓7月反對維持利率的主張重新增強。

貝森特承諾的措施，仍須看細節與實際結果。荷莫茲持續通航、運費與保險成本下降，及油價回吐近週漲幅，都可舒緩壓力；若限制實際削減出口，或再有軍事干擾，7月生產者能源與物流降價便較像過去式。2年期殖利率與10年期通膨補償同步上升，意味能源進入政策預期；若短端穩定、曲線轉陡，負擔就更多落在長期補償。

週三$160億20年期美債標售，是下一場直接需求測試。該券週五約在5.25%交易，發行前市場指示約5.27%；若在附近得標，將創2020年重新推出該年期以來最高，目前尚無結果。相對自身標售前利率的得標表現與後續交易，可看出投資人是否接受當前價格。若得標利率明顯偏高，或曲線再度轉陡，代表單靠公司債發行放緩，尚不足以減輕政府借款與AI投資的資金競爭。

overall_summary.summary: 零售疲弱一度讓2年期殖利率跌破4.10%，對伊朗施壓卻推升油價、逆轉行情。10年期收盤上升5個基點至4.68%，信用市場投資人也更重視定價。

section_summaries.section_title: 消費轉弱，仍未能壓住收盤殖利率
section_summaries.summary: 消費疲弱先支持美債，油價卻逆轉漲勢。信用買方手中仍有現金，但不願接受過窄的最終利差。

section_summaries.section_title: 消費降溫，油價與長期借款成本卻形成反向壓力
section_summaries.summary: 零售與信心降低近期升息定價，Goolsbee仍要持續通膨改善。油價推升通膨補償與實質殖利率，長期融資依然昂貴。

section_summaries.section_title: 信用買家手上有錢，但要求保留新券溢價

long_thesis.english_markdown:
# Oil reverses the Treasury rally as credit buyers resist tighter pricing

## Weak spending cannot hold yields down

Treasuries initially rallied on weak retail sales and consumer sentiment, then reversed as new US threats against Iran lifted oil. The two-year yield briefly fell below 4.10%, its lowest since June 30, but finished 2 basis points higher at 4.17%. Five-, ten- and 30-year yields rose 4, 5 and 4 basis points to 4.36%, 4.68% and 5.25%. The curve steepened, with 2s10s up 3 basis points to 51 and 2s30s up 2 to 108.

July retail sales fell 0.6%, the largest decline since May 2025, and preliminary August consumer sentiment missed expectations at 51. Goolsbee favored patience as inflation improved. Those developments reduced the immediate case for a Fed increase, but Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's promise of unprecedented economic pressure on Iran shifted attention back to energy. WTI rose 1.42% to $82.40 and Brent 1.67% to $88.52. Ten-year breakevens gained 3 basis points to 2.27%, while real yields rose 2 to 2.41%.

Credit investors were also resisting lower compensation after a crowded calendar. Investment-grade borrowers had raised $136 billion in two weeks. Average orders fell 36% from initial books as syndicates tightened final prices, twice the prior week's attrition and above the 22% annual average. Funds still attracted nearly $3 billion and spreads remained near 78 basis points. The problem was not a shortage of cash, but how much concession buyers would give up.

That negotiation extends beyond conventional bonds. AI financing increasingly relies on guarantees that could bring losses back to chipmakers during a downturn; Zenith Arc's data-center deal priced at the wide end despite a long Jane Street lease. Other borrowers turned to equity or challenged collateral transfers. Markets continued to provide financing, but its terms increasingly depended on which balance sheet would ultimately bear the loss.

## Consumers weaken; oil and long borrowing costs push back

Five of the 13 retail categories declined in July. Non-store sales, including online purchases, fell 2.2% and motor vehicles and parts 1.8%. Restaurants and bars, the report's only service category, rose 0.5%. The figures are not inflation-adjusted, and Amazon's shift of Prime Day from July last year to June this year may have pulled online spending forward. Even allowing for that timing effect, the report showed less consumer resilience after a stronger first half.

The University of Michigan's preliminary sentiment reading of 51 compared with a consensus of 55. Together with softer hiring and the week's inflation reports, the releases extended the policy repricing begun on August 7. Short-rate contracts priced about 8 basis points of September tightening, down from nearly 19 on July 31. Traders were also moving away from more than one increase by mid-2027. The early two-year rally reflected a real change in the expected path, even though it did not survive the session.

Goolsbee described the economy and labor market as basically stable, while saying a sustained, multi-month decline in retail sales would make him nervous. Inflation remains his main concern. He welcomed improvement over the past three months after five or six unfavorable months and said another three or four readings like June would give him more confidence in a return to 2%. July's fifth consecutive hold still drew three dissents favoring a quarter-point increase; one weak spending report has not settled the debate.

He also questioned whether slower productivity after last year's strength would prove temporary. AI could increase supply capacity and lower unit costs, but its investment boom could simultaneously overheat demand. That leaves the Fed assessing both future efficiency gains and current spending on equipment, power and construction rather than treating technology as uniformly disinflationary.

Bessent said measures to be announced the following week would be unprecedented in the history of economic isolation, alongside the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports. The comments arrived before the close and reversed the benefit of weaker consumption. Brent finished 5.95% higher over a week and WTI 5.40% higher. The 3-basis-point breakeven rise more than reversed Thursday's decline and returned the ten-year measure to its August 11 level; higher real yields added a second source of pressure.

Longer borrowing costs remained elevated after the week's auctions. The 30-year closed above its 5.216% auction yield, while the ten-year returned almost to its own sale's clearing level. Over a month, ten- and 30-year nominal yields are up 10 and 17 basis points, against a 1-basis-point decline at two years. The 2s30s curve has steepened 18 basis points. Ten-year real yields are up 8 basis points at 2.41%; 30-year real yields are up 13 at 3.00%.

The auctions established demand at high prices for the borrower, not a cure for deficits or growing private investment needs. Treasury has discussed possible changes to issuance, but has not reduced long-bond supply. Shifting more debt to two- through seven-year maturities would alter duration and refinancing exposure, not the total borrowing requirement.

Total Treasury turnover was $974.5 billion in original-face value, down 19.0% from Thursday, with nominal coupons accounting for $824.4 billion. Activity beyond 20 years nevertheless rose 3.3% to $116.8 billion, and dealer-to-customer trades made up 50.7% of that bucket. Long yields rose with continued participation rather than simply a lack of trading.

Equities were less affected by the energy reversal. The S&P 500 fell 0.17% and Nasdaq 100 0.13%, while VIX declined 2.60% to 14.25. Gold gained 0.39% to $4,380.40 and the Dollar Index fell 0.29% to 99.67. Bonds absorbed more of the renewed inflation concern without a broad dollar squeeze or equity retreat.

## Credit buyers keep their cash, but demand a concession

Order attrition made the change in primary-market behavior visible. The week's 36% average was 14 percentage points above the 2026 norm, and Thursday's 45% was the year's highest. Orders for AMD's longest tranche fell by more than half after the company tightened pricing in its $4.75 billion sale. The deal still cleared; the initial book was not the amount investors would accept at any spread.

The $136 billion issued over two weeks put August on course for a record, before an expected slowdown to roughly $20 billion the following week. Acquisition financing, AI infrastructure and ordinary refinancing arrived together, against a Treasury curve offering high real yields. More alternatives increased the opportunity cost of accepting minimal new-issue compensation.

High-grade funds received almost $3 billion in the week through Wednesday, and average spreads were near 78 basis points. HYG and JNK declined only 0.10% and 0.07% Friday and remained slightly positive over a week. LQD fell 0.40% as benchmark yields rose. These returns were far from general liquidation; the more revealing question was how much demand remained when issuers removed spread from their initial offers.

Zenith Arc supplied a project-level example. Its $2.25 billion five-year Ba2 green bonds priced at 99.5 to yield almost 9%, at the wide end of earlier discussion. A Jane Street subsidiary's 15-year triple-net lease and customary group guarantee assign operating expenses, taxes, utilities, insurance and power costs to the tenant. Even with that support, investors required the wider end of the proposed range for construction, technology and concentration exposure.

## AI guarantees can return losses to the supplier

Nvidia's proposed partnership with Goldman Sachs, Blackstone and Apollo aims to enable as much as $500 billion of computing investment. Huang has described residual-value support of up to 25% of an opportunity, assessed case by case. That limit bounds the commitment to each project, but the risks become intertwined when customers cannot pay and equipment loses value together.

An SPV can borrow against equipment and contracts at a lower cost with a residual-value backstop. If the customer stops paying, the hardware can be re-leased or sold, and the guarantor covers any remaining shortfall. Debt amortizes as chips depreciate, often over roughly five years, reducing the guarantee. Yet the protection matters most when defaults and falling resale values coincide—the same downturn likely to weaken the chipmaker's earnings.

Meta used residual-value support in approximately $27 billion of financing for Hyperion in Louisiana and a roughly $13 billion Sopaipilla package in Texas, linked to choosing to leave long leases early. Broadcom backstopped most of the $35 billion Big Sky chip financing for Anthropic. Bank of America strategists estimated that the broader AI XPV platform could accumulate $370 billion of senior debt by mid-2029. These are different structures and conditions, not interchangeable corporate debt balances.

S&P treats Broadcom's support as a contingent debt-like obligation in adjusted leverage. Moody's warned that several transactions in a short period could reduce financial flexibility even if reported debt stays low. Roughly $70 billion of this contingent support already sits outside major companies' reported debt. During expansion it helps customers fund purchases with little immediate cash cost to the supplier; in a downturn it can bring losses back just as earnings and equipment values deteriorate. Credit analysis therefore has to consider the correlation among customers, collateral and guarantors, not only the amount of bonds formally outstanding.

## Collateral disputes and equity deals redistribute creditor risk

Arini and GoldenTree expanded their Liberty Puerto Rico lawsuit to challenge a $140 million revolver and $200 million term loan agreed in May. They allege the facilities were secured by assets moved to an unrestricted subsidiary in a September liability-management exercise. The earlier transaction put most assets beyond existing lenders' reach to support $250 million of new Diameter Capital Partners debt, according to the creditors. AllianceBernstein affiliates, Octagon Credit Investors and MacKay Shields joined the case in New York Supreme Court.

The amended complaint also cites an intercompany loan canceled without consideration and $500 million of preferred equity issued in May that could pay Liberty Latin America shareholders $45 million in annual dividends. These are contested allegations about relocated collateral, payment priority and shareholder distributions, not a court ruling. The case tests how far unrestricted-subsidiary provisions and new financing can alter recoveries for legacy lenders.

Dangote Sugar instead used equity to repair its balance sheet. It raised NGN486 billion, or $356 million, in an oversubscribed rights issue, placing 8.1 billion shares at NGN60 each. The money will reduce debt, restore capital depleted by three years of losses and fund operations and backward integration. Nigeria's 2023 devaluation increased financing and input costs and had pushed the company into negative equity before a recovery. Existing shareholders accept dilution to strengthen the resources available to the business and its creditors.

Kedrion Biopharma is considering a different use of capital: about €2 billion of private debt, partly to pay owners including Permira and Abu Dhabi Investment Authority. The plasma-therapy company generates more than €1.5 billion of revenue, but terms and a final decision remain under discussion. Abundant private-lender cash after a prolonged acquisition drought may support the transaction. A sponsor distribution, however, would leave a different creditor cushion than an equivalent amount raised for productive expansion; the final leverage and documentation still matter.

## Indonesia promises a smaller deficit; China relies on public borrowing

Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto targeted a 2027 deficit of 2.4% of GDP, down from an expected 2.85% in 2026. Spending would rise 4% to IDR4,097 trillion and revenue 7%, with assumptions of IDR17,500 per dollar and $75 crude. The rupiah and stocks rose and bond yields fell on Friday.

The lower deficit still depends on delivery. First-half government spending rose almost 30% and helped produce 5.45% growth, the strongest first-half result in 13 years. Last year's deficit target had already been revised toward the 3% legal ceiling. Procurement savings, state-enterprise dividends and revenue growth must now pay for food, energy, education and village programs without another upward revision. The published target is supportive; it is not evidence that the savings have already occurred.

Kenya plans an $815 million Eurobond by end-December within a $5.4 billion external-financing program through June 2027. The package also includes a $300 million panda bond, $500 million sukuk and $1 billion debt-for-food swap with the World Food Programme, backed by the US International Development Finance Corporation. Treasury Secretary John Mbadi also intends to retire at least $500 million of expensive external debt. With the IMF classifying Kenya at high risk of debt distress, replacing costly liabilities matters alongside obtaining new money.

China's financing data showed public borrowing replacing weak private demand. The real economy net repaid CNY590 billion of local-currency loans in July, the largest contraction in data back to 2002. Overall loans, including interfinancial credit, fell CNY340 billion, more than three times the expected decline. Aggregate financing still increased CNY1.4 trillion, but government bonds accounted for CNY1.3 trillion. Both household and corporate longer-term loans contracted as weak property demand, stagnant wages and low expected returns encouraged deleveraging.

The PBOC used CNY349 billion of overnight reverse repos, a net CNY348 billion injection and its first mid-month use of that tenor. This addressed tax-payment demand after it skipped other open-market additions, rather than announcing a broad easing shift. A separate CNY1 trillion six-month outright reverse repo simply replaced an equal maturity. China's ten-year government yield fell 1 basis point to 1.68%, its lowest since July 2025, and a ten-year auction achieved its lowest yield in more than a year. Precise funding support can stabilize money markets without reversing the record weakness in private borrowing.

## Sanctions details and the 20-year auction follow the reversal

Core PCE on August 26, intervening employment evidence and Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks will show whether the favorable inflation sequence is becoming long enough to satisfy Goolsbee. Continued demand weakness, tame service prices and softer hiring would support policy-sensitive maturities even if long funding stays expensive. Stronger spending or broader inflation would give renewed force to July's dissents.

Bessent's promised measures require details and physical outcomes. Sustained Hormuz passage, cheaper freight and insurance, and oil reversing its weekly advance would ease pressure. Restrictions that materially reduce exports or further military disruption would instead leave July's lower producer energy and logistics costs looking backward. Joint increases in two-year yields and ten-year breakevens would suggest energy entering policy expectations; a stable front end with a steeper curve would place more of the burden in longer-term compensation.

Wednesday's $16 billion 20-year Treasury auction is the next direct demand test. The bond traded around 5.25% Friday, with a when-issued indication near 5.27%. An award around that level would be the highest since the tenor's 2020 reintroduction; no result is yet available. The award relative to its own pre-sale yield and subsequent trading will show whether investors accept the duration at current prices. A tail or renewed steepening would suggest that slower corporate issuance alone is insufficient to relieve competition from government borrowing and AI investment.
